title: From Endomorphism to Galois Generator
content: The parent entry exhibited the Frobenius $x \mapsto x^p$ as a ring **endomorphism** in characteristic $p$. This file upgrades it to **Galois theory**: over the prime field $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p$ the Frobenius is a field *automorphism* fixing $\mathbb{F}_p$, hence an element $\mathrm{frob} \in \mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{F}_p) = K \simeq_{\mathrm{alg}}[\mathbb{Z}/p]\, K$. That group is **cyclic** of order $n = [K:\mathbb{F}_p]$, and $\mathrm{frob}$ generates it. Mathlib supplies the finite-field Galois machinery for an arbitrary finite base; the contribution here is to specialise it to the prime base — where the abstract $|\text{base}|$-power map becomes the honest $x \mapsto x^p$ — and to assemble the explicit structure theorem $\mathrm{Gal}(\mathbb{F}_{p^n}/\mathbb{F}_p) \cong \mathbb{Z}/n$.

title: frob: the Frobenius as a Galois automorphism
content: `frob` is defined as `FiniteField.frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic (ZMod p) K`, Mathlib's $|\text{base}|$-power automorphism of an algebraic extension, packaged as an element of $K \simeq_{\mathrm{alg}}[\mathbb{Z}/p]\, K$. The base is the prime field $\mathbb{Z}/p$, with $|\mathbb{Z}/p| = p$, so the underlying map is $x \mapsto x^p$ — the same map as the parent endomorphism, but now realised as an invertible algebra automorphism rather than a mere ring homomorphism.

title: The prime base collapses to x ↦ x^p
content: `frob_apply`: the Galois-theoretic Frobenius acts as the honest prime Frobenius $x \mapsto x^p$. The abstract construction is the $|\text{base}|$-power map; over $\mathbb{Z}/p$ the base has exactly $\mathrm{Fintype.card}\,(\mathbb{Z}/p) = p$ elements, so a single rewrite with `ZMod.card` identifies the Galois generator with the parent entry's prime Frobenius. The automorphism and the endomorphism are literally the same map — now invertible.

title: Order = group order = dimension
content: Three quantities all equal $n$: `orderOf_frob` gives $\mathrm{ord}(\mathrm{frob}) = \mathrm{finrank}_{\mathbb{F}_p} K$ (Mathlib's `orderOf_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic`); `card_galoisGroup` gives $|\mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{F}_p)| = \mathrm{finrank}_{\mathbb{F}_p} K$ (`IsGalois.card_aut_eq_finrank`, the `IsGalois` and `FiniteDimensional` instances being automatic for finite extensions of finite fields); and `isCyclic_galoisGroup` records that the group is cyclic via `inferInstance`. The coincidence of the first two is exactly what will force the Frobenius to generate.

title: Equal cardinalities force generation
content: `zpowers_frob_eq_top` proves $\langle \mathrm{frob} \rangle = \top$ via `Subgroup.card_eq_iff_eq_top`: it suffices that $|\langle \mathrm{frob} \rangle| = |\mathrm{Gal}|$. The left side is $\mathrm{ord}(\mathrm{frob})$ (`Nat.card_zpowers`), which equals $n$ (`orderOf_frob`), which equals the group order (`card_galoisGroup`) — so the whole proof is a four-rewrite chain. `mem_zpowers_frob` and `exists_pow_frob` then express the consequence: every automorphism is an integer (resp. natural-number) power of the Frobenius.

title: Order exactly n: the iterate returns, but not before
content: `frob_pow_finrank`: $\mathrm{frob}^n = 1$ by `pow_orderOf_eq_one` after rewriting with `orderOf_frob`. `frob_iterate_finrank`: pointwise $(\mathrm{frob})^{[n]} x = x^{p^n} = x$, a `calc` chaining `coe_frobeniusAlgEquivOfAlgebraic_iterate` (the $n$-fold iterate is $x \mapsto x^{p^n}$), `pow_finrank_eq_card` ($p^n = |K|$), and `FiniteField.pow_card` ($x^{|K|} = x$). `frob_pow_ne_one`: for $0 < m < n$ no power is the identity, via `orderOf_le_of_pow_eq_one` and `omega` — sharpness of the order.

title: The explicit structure theorem Gal ≅ ℤ/n
content: `galoisGroupMulEquivZMod` transports `zmodCyclicMulEquiv` (for any cyclic $G$, an explicit $\mathrm{Multiplicative}(\mathbb{Z}/|G|) \simeq^* G$) along `card_galoisGroup` to give a concrete isomorphism $\mathrm{Multiplicative}(\mathbb{Z}/n) \simeq^* \mathrm{Gal}(K/\mathbb{F}_p)$ sending the additive generator $1$ to the Frobenius. Rather than merely asserting cyclicity, this exhibits the full structure theorem — from which the subfield lattice (subgroups of $\mathbb{Z}/n \leftrightarrow$ divisors of $n$) reads off immediately.
